ApiError.description: What a route answers when it cannot do what was asked (a 400).

source.description: `keychain`: handed over by the Mac app from the macOS Keychain.

ApiKeyStatus.description: The active provider's key state, with where keys are kept (`GET /api/settings`).

upstreamUrl.description: The project this one began as a fork of; shown as credit, never used as a feed.

ConfigRequest.description: The save to use (`POST /api/config`): its CSV export folder and its name.

lgPath.description: Diagnostic: where the `.lg` was found. Not something the user has to supply.

simulatedThrough.description: Last simulated in-game date (ISO), from the save itself.

currentDate.description: `leagues.current_date` of the imported export (ISO): the day about to be played.

simulatedThrough.description: The last day the imported data reflects.

ExportPendingEvent.description: OOTP has written a fresh export the server has not imported yet.

through.description: Simulated-through date on the common basis, ISO.
Simulated-through date on the common basis, ISO.

headline.description: One line, e.g. "Partial — transaction log 1 day behind".

action.description: What the user should do about it, when there is something to do.

GameDate.description: An in-game date as the server serves it. A string, never a date type: OOTP writes dates unpadded (`2026-5-9`), and although the fields that pass through `parseGameDate` are padded, a client compares or orders game dates only as the server does (D-056). The contract (`contract/openapi.json`) names it `GameDate`, with no format.

HelloEvent.description: The first event on every stream: the `/api/status` snapshot, so nothing is missed between loading and listening.

ImportAccepted.description: What `POST /api/import` answers: the import has started; its progress and result arrive on `/api/status` and the event stream.

table.description: The table being written, as OOTP names the file.

fileIndex.description: 1-based, so it reads as "12 of 70" without arithmetic.

rows.description: Rows written so far, across every table.

ImportProgress.description: Where the import has got to, for a page that would rather not look frozen.

Integer.description: A whole number: an id, a count, a season, a number of days. The spec says `type: integer`, so the Mac app reads an `Int`, not a `Double`. A true decimal (a rate, a slider, dollars) stays `number`. Named `Integer`, never `Int`, which the Swift generator would rename.

JobEvent.description: A background job (storylines, the briefing) changed state for one club.

source.description: `keychain`: handed over by the Mac app from the macOS Keychain.

lastTransactionDate.description: The newest date on any transaction row.

activityThrough.description: The newest date on any day-stamped table in the database.

coveredThrough.description: How far the database has demonstrably been written. Days with no transactions (off-season, an off-day) leave `lastTransactionDate` behind without the log being behind, so this takes the newest of everything.

found.description: The live transaction database exists in the save's temp folder.

Ok.description: A request the server accepted, with nothing more to say.

Org.description: A major-league club as `GET /api/orgs` lists it.

mode.description: V1 uses manual. Staff and hybrid exist now so V2 can be introduced without changing the persisted shape.

manual.description: User-selected values. Always available as a fallback.

overrides.description: In hybrid mode these dimensions stay user-controlled while the others may come from staff.

ProviderChoice.description: A provider on offer, with the model it would use (`GET /api/settings/providers`).

ProviderId.description:
Four ways to reach a model, behind one shape.

The app was written against Anthropic and every feature still works best there — the chat's tool loop and prompt caching are Anthropic's shapes, and this is where they stay. What this adds is a choice for anyone who already pays for a key somewhere else, which is most of the reason people asked.

Only the parts that genuinely differ are adapted. A system prompt is a separate argument at Anthropic, the first message at OpenAI, and its own field at Google; a refusal is a stop reason, a field on the message, and a finish reason respectively. Those are normalised here so the four call sites upstream never learn which provider answered.

ProviderInfo.description: One AI service the app can talk to, as the Settings screen lists it.

ProvidersResponse.description: What `GET /api/settings/providers` serves: the providers on offer and every provider's key state.

ResolveFolderRequest.description: The folder the user picked or typed (`POST /api/resolve-folder`).

saves.description: Saves found inside the chosen folder, when it holds several.

SaveList.description: The saves found in the usual places (`GET /api/saves`).

SaveSourceRequest.description: The `<save>.lg` folder named by hand (`POST /api/save-source`); empty or null returns to automatic.

SaveSourceResult.description: What `POST /api/save-source` answers once the save folder is set or cleared.

SearchLocation.description: One place the server looks for saves: a human label, the folder, and whether it exists here.

SearchLocations.description: Where `GET /api/search-locations` looked for saves, so the user can see why auto-detection came up empty.

ServerEvent.description:
What the server tells a connected app as it happens, over `GET /api/v2/events` (server-sent events, D-055).

The React app polls `/api/status` every few seconds; the Mac app listens here instead. Every event is a fact the server already holds (the same fields `/api/status` and the job routes serve), pushed when it changes. An event is a nudge to re-read, never a second source of truth: a client that missed one reads `/api/status`, and the stream opens with a `hello` carrying that snapshot so nothing is missed between loading and listening.

The names are the contract's (N2 describes them in `contract/openapi.json`); a client ignores a name it does not know, so new events can be added without breaking an older app.

app.description: Product name and version, from package.json (see appInfo.ts).

importProgress.description: Where a running import has got to; null when nothing is importing.

importInterruptedSince.description: Set when an import stopped partway (the server was stopped or crashed); cleared by the next completed import.

exportPending.description: Set when OOTP has written a fresh export the app has not imported yet.

logoToken.description: Changes with the save, and rides along on every logo URL.

ratingScaleMax.description: The top of the rating scale the save shows ratings on.

ServerStatus.description: What `/api/status` serves, and the snapshot `/api/v2/events` opens with (described in `contract/openapi.json`).

theme.description: 'system' follows the OS setting and changes with it.

model.description: Model id used by every AI feature. See models.ts for the picker's list.

provider.description: Which service the AI features talk to. Anthropic unless changed — it is what the app was built against and the only one the chat's tool loop and prompt caching are native to.

models.description: The model chosen for each provider, remembered separately. Switching provider would otherwise leave a model id the new one has never heard of.

aiFeatures.description:
Optional provider/model overrides for individual AI workloads.

Missing entries inherit the global provider and that provider's selected model, preserving the behaviour of existing settings files.

roundRatingsToFive.description: Write overall and potential in fives, the way scouts talk. Display only — sorting and every calculation keep the exact grade.

showUnavailablePitchers.description:
Keep pitchers on the injured list in the bullpen table.

Off unless asked for. That page answers one question — who can throw tonight — and a man six weeks from a rehab start is not an answer to it. Nothing vanishes quietly: the heading says how many are being held back and hands them over in a click.

autoGenerateAfterImport.description:
Write the storylines and the briefing by themselves after each import.

Off unless asked for. Both cost money on someone else's API key, and a setting that quietly spends it would be a poor default however convenient.

nextSeasonBudget.description:
What you expect the owner to hand you next season, per club, in dollars.

OOTP does not publish a future budget — it is not set until the offseason — so future headroom had to assume this year's holds flat. On a club whose budget swings, that is the wrong number to plan against, and you are the one who knows which way the owner leans. Absent an entry, flat it stays.

organizationPhilosophies.description: Organizational philosophy is saved per club. The string key is the OOTP organization/team id so different clubs and saves may think differently.

Settings.description:
User preferences, plus the Anthropic API key.

The key is a real secret, so it is never written in plain text when we can avoid it: the desktop app hands us Electron's safeStorage, which encrypts against the OS keychain (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows). Running from source in a browser there is no keychain available, so the key falls back to a 0600 file and the UI says so plainly rather than implying it is protected.

shmPresent.description: Whether the source had a `-shm` file. It is never copied.

sourceModified.description: Modification times of the source files when copied.

UnknownServerEvent.description: An event this build of the contract does not name, sent by a newer server. The spec lists it last among `ServerEvent`'s shapes, so an older app decodes it (and ignores it) instead of failing the stream.
